name: The Synagogue System and the Sanhedrin

objectives.text: Identify a synagogue as a place where Jewish people gathered on the Sabbath to hear God's Word read and to pray
Retell how Jesus went to the synagogue in Nazareth on the Sabbath and read from the scroll of Isaiah
Name the people who served in a synagogue, such as the ruler who led the gathering and the attendant who cared for the scrolls
Summarize the main parts of a synagogue gathering, including reading the Law and the Prophets, teaching, and prayer
Explain the difference between the Temple in Jerusalem as the one place of sacrifice and the synagogues in many towns as places of reading, teaching, and prayer
Identify the Sanhedrin as the ruling council of the Jews in Jerusalem, led by the high priest
Explain how Ezra's public reading and explanation of the Law gave a pattern for reading and teaching Scripture in the synagogue
Compare the role of a synagogue ruler with the role of a priest serving in the Temple
Explain what Jesus meant when he said the scribes and Pharisees sit on the seat of Moses
Describe how Jesus and Paul used the synagogue as a setting to teach Scripture and proclaim the gospel
Analyze the Sanhedrin's role in the trial of Jesus, including its search for testimony and its charge of blasphemy
Describe how members of the council such as Caiaphas, Nicodemus, and Joseph of Arimathea responded differently to Jesus
Explain how synagogues allowed Jews scattered in the Diaspora to keep hearing the Law and why Paul often began his mission work there
Explain what being put out of the synagogue meant and why it was a serious threat to those who confessed Jesus
Analyze how the apostles answered the Sanhedrin's command to stop preaching in the name of Jesus
Distinguish synagogue practices shown in the New Testament from customs such as the minyan that are described in later rabbinic sources
Construct a diagram of the Sanhedrin's makeup, including the high priest, chief priests, elders, and scribes and the parties represented among them
Analyze how the synagogue pattern of public reading, exhortation, and prayer shaped the worship of the early church
Evaluate the legal authority of the Sanhedrin under Roman rule, including why it brought Jesus to Pilate
Evaluate the Sanhedrin's judgment of Jesus against the Old Testament standards for just judges and reliable witnesses
Develop an account of how the synagogue's focus on Torah helped Judaism endure after the Temple fell, contrasted with the Reformed teaching that Christ fulfills the Temple

changes: Reworded the kindergarten objective to drop the inaccurate label of a synagogue as a church for Jews. Folded the rabbi objective into a fuller one on synagogue roles (ruler and attendant), with verse anchors. Dropped the observe verb in favour of a retelling objective. Kept and sharpened the service summary, the Temple and synagogue contrast, the ruler and priest comparison, the seat of Moses, the trial of Jesus, the Diaspora link, the early church worship link, the Sanhedrin diagram, and the evaluation of Jewish courts under Rome. Reframed the minyan objective as a distinction between New Testament evidence and later rabbinic sources. Replaced the vague defend and synthesize objectives with one grade 12 objective on the synagogue after AD 70 and the Reformed teaching that Christ fulfills the Temple. Added objectives on Ezra's reading as a precedent, identifying the Sanhedrin, Jesus and Paul teaching in synagogues, council members' differing responses, exclusion from the synagogue, the apostles before the council (with WCF 20.2), and judging the trial by Old Testament standards of justice. Added WCF 21.5 and WSC Q89 where the doctrine of public reading and preaching applies. Left sect beliefs, feasts, and messianic hopes to the sibling sub-topics.
